CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
45-year-old male presents with right ankle injury sustained while playing basketball with his son at the courts. Patient went up for a shot and was contacted by his son while in the air. Upon landing, patient rolled and twisted the ankle. Patient reports pain on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient has had difficulty walking and reports the ankle does not feel stable. Patient recently returned to a regular exercise routine and is concerned about disruption to his fitness goals. Patient also volunteers to coach starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. Patient plays basketball with his 10-year-old son Sean, who plays basketball. Patient has a dog. Patient recently returned to regular gym workouts.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right ankle examination reveals significant swelling on the lateral side. Exquisite tenderness on the lateral aspect of the ankle. Some tenderness over the medial deltoid region. Skin intact with no epidermolysis. Brisk capillary refill noted. No malalignment. Patient able to stand on ankle but reports pain with weight-bearing and sensation of instability.

RESULTS
Right ankle X-ray (AP, lateral, and oblique views) shows displaced lateral malleolus fracture at the Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolus fracture, right ankle. Patient will require surgical intervention with plate and screw fixation. Patient to be provided crutches. Prescribed meloxicam for pain and inflammation management. Patient instructed to ice ankle and keep it elevated. Expected recovery time approximately three months. Patient may continue coaching starting in April. Patient will resume exercise after three-month recovery period.
